chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about the female slave (concubine) whose master dies concerning her, and he said: Her husband observes the waiting period (ʿiddah) of the one who died concerning her.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a female slave whose master dies?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam Ibrahim al-Imam clarifies that upon the master's death, the female slave (umm al-walad) observes the full three-month waiting period (ʿiddah al-mawt) of a free wife, rather than the shorter period for a concubine. This ruling underscores her elevated status in inheritance and marital ties, reflecting the Shia juristic view that manumission or the master's death elevates her legal standing to that of a wife for the purpose of ʿiddah.
